§9.1.3 Empty Pre-Printed Grids

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-empty-pre-printed-grids · tables forms degenerate

✅ Normative

A printed grid with no values entered MUST be rendered as a table, with its headers and every printed empty row as a row of empty cells. It MUST NOT be skipped, and MUST NOT be reduced to its headers alone.

A blank form table — full ruled structure, headers printed, no values entered anywhere.

| Name | Date | Amount | Signature |
|      |      |        |           |
|      |      |        |           |

Requirements

  • The grid MUST be rendered as a table. The headers are the content: they are what the form asks for.
  • Every printed empty row MUST be rendered, as empty cells. An empty cell is a cell.
  • The headers MUST NOT be emitted on their own. A headers-only output is the degenerate shape ruled out in Header-Only Tables§9.1.4; here the printed empty rows are the body, so keeping them avoids that shape.
  • The table MUST NOT be skipped because it has no data. A page with a printed form on it is not blank.
  • A long run of identical empty rows — dozens of them — MUST be rendered in full, never trimmed to a representative few.

✅ Sample — xx

An NAIC rate-filing exhibit where every row after the first is a blank template row awaiting entry — the structure is the content. Each blank row still prints XX and the computed 0.00% / 0.00 subtotals, and all nine are kept. Each column header is one label wrapped over many lines, so its lines are joined into one cell, including the words broken mid-word by the narrow columns.

Why

A reader of a blank form is asking "what fields does this form ask for?", and the structure answers that question completely. Returning nothing gives nothing for a page that is manifestly not blank.

The row count is the awkward part: reproducing forty empty rows is faithful and repetitive, reproducing one is compact and unfaithful. Faithful wins — trimming cannot be undone downstream, while ignoring extra empty rows can be (never drop).

✅ Sample — a court scheduling order

SCHEDULING AND CUTOFF DATES: three columns, nine rows, every row's description printed and its two date cells empty. The banner above the header row is a title band inside the frame.
